messages:
Chandra: thinking about adding a lightweight 'gating' block to runtime config so we can auto-pause or rollback rollouts when telemetry crosses thresholds. sketch of API below — want to capture p95/error/quality signals, but keep it simple and auditable. any obvious missing pieces?

Chandra: ```json
{
  "gate_id": "gate-release-2026-03",
  "scope": { "routes": ["/v1/generate"], "models": ["gptx-7b"] },
  "conditions": [
    { "metric": "p95_latency_ms", "comparison": "gt", "threshold": 600, "window_sec": 300 },
    { "metric": "error_rate", "comparison": "gt", "threshold": 0.015, "window_sec": 300 }
  ],
  "on_trigger": { "action": "pause", "notify": ["eng-oncall"] },
  "dry_run": true,
  "safety_window_sec": 900
}
```

Matt: :eyes: looks reasonable. couple q's:
- where does model-quality (eval) fit? we have callback evals that run nightly. can gating consume a quality signal?
- how do we avoid noisy single-minute blips causing flaps? safety_window helps but maybe add a min-duration or require N/3 windows?

Alice: UX note — console should show gate state inline with rollout timeline. small badge: ACTIVE / DRY_RUN / PAUSED, and a 1-click 'force-promote' or 'hold' button + link to last 15m metrics for the gate. also show which metric tripped and when.

Ben: sampling/telemetry question: if we use sampled traces for p95, the p95 might jitter depending on sampling rate. we should either use service-side aggregated p95 with consistent sampling or use p99 of error-rate for safety. also, how does this interact with quota-based fallbacks? if quota kicks users to a cheaper model, gated route might show different metrics.

Chandra: good pts — plan: allow gating conditions to reference named telemetry streams (e.g., "ingress_p95", "model_quality_eval") managed by telemetry team. gating engine evaluates on aggregated series (not ad-hoc sampled traces). default evaluation = 1m cadence with a sliding window.

Oliver: minor API suggestion: add an explicit "escalate_to" field so that on trigger we can route traffic to fallback model (route-by-cost/fallback) instead of full pause. e.g., "on_trigger": { "action": "fallback", "target": "gptx-3b" }

ConfigBot: automated note — created draft config: gate-release-2026-03 in staging. dry_run=true. eval window=300s.

Sara: I'll prototype the backend evaluator and a small console card next week. can we define the telemetry names and a minimal schema? I can mock metrics if needed.

Ben: agree on telemetry naming. also propose we add a small hysteresis config: "min_consecutive_failures": 2 and "cooldown_sec": 600 to avoid thrash.

Alice: UX: when dry_run=true console should show an "Observed triggers" list (so PMs can approve). also a button to promote dry_run->active with one click + audit modal.

Chandra: updated plan:
- gating config references telemetry streams by name
- evaluator runs on aggregated series, 60s cadence, default window 300s
- actions: pause / fallback / notify / escalate
- safety: min_consecutive_failures, cooldown_sec, safety_window_sec
- dry_run shows observed triggers but doesn't change routing

Matt: ok, next steps: doc the API, get telemetry owners to expose named streams, Sara to prototype evaluator, Alice to mock console card. i'll open a design RFC + link PR.

Oliver: adding: check quota interactions in RFC — if fallback hits quota we'll need a secondary fallback or forced slowdown.

Chandra: thanks all. tagging follow-ups: @Sara to prototype, @Alice to mock, @Matt to RFC, @Ben to define hysteresis defaults. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/1021 (WIP). :thumbsup:

Matt: :thumbsup:

Alice: :+1: will mock a small card and add acceptance criteria (audit trail, promote button, observed triggers).

Sara: will start a staging job tomorrow and post logs in this thread.

Ben: :robot_face: can telemetry team add the named streams by EOD?

ConfigBot: note — staging job started: jobs/24892. logs: https://staging.redwood/logs/24892

Chandra: awesome. leaving this open for a bit for any late concerns. if no blockers we'll lock API next Tue and start implementation. :warning:
